wiki_text: Since 2023 Sonatrach has been running a large-scale modernization program at its Arzew liquefaction complexes aimed at restoring throughput rather than adding nameplate capacity. Reporting in 2024-2025 describes lifting GL1Z and GL2Z utilization from roughly 60% toward 100%, with combined output targeted at about 11 million tonnes per year (up from a reduced ~6.6 Mt/yr). The work includes replacing four main cryogenic heat exchangers (MCHEs) at GL1Z under a contract originally signed with Air Products and assumed by Honeywell after its September 2024 acquisition of Air Products' LNG process-technology business. Nominal per-complex capacity is unchanged: GL1Z 7.9 mtpa and GL2Z 8.2 mtpa (six trains each, GL1Z commissioned 1978). These are output/utilization gains, not new liquefaction capacity.

Skikda's single operating liquefaction train (the ~4.5 mtpa 'megatrain' that entered service in 2013, replacing the trains destroyed in the January 2004 explosion) returned from an extended scheduled-maintenance shutdown on 19 October 2025. Sonatrach described the outage as part of its 2025-2030 Infrastructure Rehabilitation Plan, covering compressor modernization, safety-system replacement and flaring-reduction upgrades. The terminal continues to operate at 4.5 mtpa.

Reported LNG storage capacity for GL1K differs by source: Sonatrach's current GL1K complex page reportedly cites 246,000 m3 while the GIIGNL 2025 Annual Report lists 150,000 m3. The figure should be reconciled directly against the primary Sonatrach source before being cited.
